summary: The note examines how e-commerce growth is pressuring local retail businesses and how they are adapting. It cites Dr. Amanda Liu's forecast that e-commerce could reach 65% of retail transactions by 2028, and describes responses such as online pivots, hyperlocal platforms, pooled technology resources, predictive analytics, loyalty programs and 'shop local' campaigns. It concludes that competition will depend less on channel and more on understanding consumer preferences.
one_line: E-commerce is squeezing local retailers, who are responding with online pivots, predictive analytics, personalization, shared resources and shop-local campaigns.
key_facts: A study released October 12, 2023 by Dr. Amanda Liu of the Local Economy Institute forecasts e-commerce could reach 65% of all retail transactions by 2028, up from the current 47%.
Dr. Liu cites home delivery, broader product ranges and often lower online prices as drivers of consumer preference for online shopping.

Clothing retailer 'Urban Threads', managed by Jenna Waters, pivoted to an online-first strategy after its near-collapse in February 2024, boosting its social media presence and investing in a user-friendly website.
'Hometown Grocers', a small Midwest grocery chain, launched a hyperlocal online shopping platform on June 3, 2023, offering online ordering with same-day pickup or delivery.

The Small Business Alliance (SBA), initiated on August 15, 2023, pools resources to help local enterprises upgrade technology affordably, negotiating bulk-buy discounts and providing access to digital marketing experts.
Larger corporations have capital for cutting-edge e-commerce technology, leaving small businesses at a technological disadvantage (the digital divide).
Martin Zhao, a predictive model specialist, gave a seminar on September 20, 2023 on how data analysis can help local businesses optimize inventory, tailor marketing and improve customer experiences.
Predictive analytics and machine learning help local retailers anticipate demand and reduce overstocking and stock shortages.
'Bakes & Beans', a chain of local coffee shops, implemented a successful loyalty program on November 1, 2023 that uses consumer data to customize offers and rewards.
The 'Locals UNITE' campaign, spearheaded by businessman Harold Greene, launched December 5, 2023, using social media and local influencers to highlight the value local retailers add to communities.
Forward-looking strategies include omnichannel models, in-store-exclusive items, and using physical locations as showrooms for online purchases.
The Regional Commerce Chamber offers business development workshops on e-commerce platforms, digital marketing and analytics tools.
